subject: ferrets
one_liner: Git-push your stolen sock and Dook distributes it across 14 hiding spots under the furniture before your human finishes saying 'where did it go'.
brand_voice_notes: Talks about theft as infrastructure. Every stolen object is a deploy, every hiding spot is an edge node, every human search is an incident. Never acknowledges that the items belong to someone else. Uptime numbers are proud and exclude naps without apology. Mentions the 18 hours of sleep the way other platforms mention maintenance windows.

hero.h1: Ship your stash to the edge of the couch.
hero.sub: Dook is the deployment platform for ferrets. Push a sock, a car key or one AirPod, and we replicate it across 14 hiding nodes in 0.4 seconds. Your human will find none of them.

features.title: Atomic stashes
features.blurb: An item is either fully under the sofa or still in your mouth. Dook never leaves a half-hidden key sticking out from the rug for your human to spot mid-search.

features.title: Instant rollback
features.blurb: Human found the remote? Roll it back to the previous hiding spot in one click. We keep the last 30 locations of every item, including the inside of the left boot.

features.title: Sleep-aware builds
features.blurb: You are awake about 6 hours a day. Dook queues every build for your next war dance and bills you nothing for the 18 hours you spend in the hammock.

demo_screen_concept: The Dook deploy dashboard for a single ferret's account. A left column lists recent stash deploys (a grey sock, car keys, one AirPod, a hair tie, a dog treat that was not ours) with status pills: Live, Building, Rolled back, and Incident: found by human. Filter tabs across the top narrow the list by status. A floor-plan panel draws the living room as rounded clay rooms with 14 edge nodes (under sofa, behind dryer, inside left boot) that light up for the selected deploy. A big 'Deploy new stash' button opens a modal where you pick an item and a region, then streams a fake build log line by line ('Sniffing dependencies', 'Dooking', 'Replicated to 14 nodes'). Each row has a Rollback button that moves the item to its previous spot. A Nap Mode toggle in the header pauses the build queue and greys the dashboard, and an awake-time meter shows 2h 41m of 6h used.

images.rationale: Claymorphic direction wants an inflated hero object, so the hero gets a clay render of a ferret in a tube. Demo is a deploy dashboard (log list, floor plan, build log), not photo-shaped, so it gets none and uses SVG clay rooms. Remaining budget goes to 3 testimonial headshots.

design_direction.style: Claymorphism, hammock-mint daylight mode. A developer-platform landing page built out of soft inflated clay: fat rounded slabs with double inner highlights and soft outer shadows, pill buttons that squish on press, and ferret-tube pipes as the connective tissue. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: ticket stubs, perforations, seat codes, fee stacks, queue strips, race bibs, split clocks, pace lines, motion slants, trail signs, blazes, contour lines, label tape, crossed-out names, middle slots, fridge magnets, ghost text, keycaps, squiggles, chrome bubbles, read receipts, sale-bill stacks, lot boxes, manicules, misregistration, activity rings, waveforms, readout chips, collar bands. Also absent: dark page backgrounds, serif type, condensed signage type, flat-only fills, hard offset shadows, paper textures. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The tube: a chunky clay ferret tunnel, mint with a darker inner shadow, that runs horizontally between sections and bends into the hero; section labels sit inside a tube opening. (2) The stash blob: stolen items drawn as small inline-SVG clay objects (sock, key, AirPod, hair tie) used as feature icons and list markers. (3) The deploy pill: every heading carries a status pill in mono ('Live · under sofa', 'Building', 'Rolled back'). (4) The nap meter: a soft clay progress capsule reading awake time out of 6h, in the nav and the highlighted tier.

fonts.body: 'DM Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

design_direction.archetype: Developer platform / hosting SaaS landing (Netlify/Vercel school): hero with product visual and terminal-ish deploy card, three features, social proof, three-tier pricing, final CTA band.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Squish and spring. Buttons scale to 0.94 on press and spring back with a cubic-bezier overshoot. Stash blobs bob 4px on a slow loop. The hero deploy card types its log lines in sequence once on load. All motion disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Two columns on desktop. Left: deploy pill, huge Baloo 2 headline in sable, sub, a coral clay CTA plus a ghost 'open the demo' pill. Right: a clay-rendered ferret photo-illustration peeking out of a mint tube, with an inflated deploy-log card overlapping its lower-left corner. A clay tube runs under the whole hero and exits stage right. Stacks to one column under 860px with the image first.
